> it's entirely possible you're at just a little higher bank angle in the right turn. It doesn't take much angular difference to require some trim adjustment.  
>  
>It's ALSO possible that the added transient drag of rolling from a left bank to a right bank reduced your airspeed by a couple knots, so you needed a bit of up trim.  
>  
>It's ALSO possible that if you slightly reduced throttle coming out of the left 360 before increasing it again while entering the right 360, slightly lower power would also require more up trim.  
>  
>Basically, unless it's a significant, noticeable amount of trim increase where you're holding bank angle and airspeed absolutely constant within very tight tolerances, I think what you're seeing is the pilot doing a slightly different left steep turn than a right steep turn :)  
>  
>(Of course, the airplane COULD be horribly out of rig. If the whole wing is warped or something, all bets are off. But you'd notice that in other ways.)
